Chapter.Content: 10 — A Production Path Tracer: Media, Randomness and Validation
Reading map · Previous chapter · Next chapter

A production path tracer must handle nested media, random streams, execution and regression evidence as well as the core estimator. This span joins those engineering contracts to implementation and profiling.
By the end: Identify the implementation and validation contracts needed for a robust path tracer.
Recall question: Which failures require a mathematical oracle, and which require scene-level tests?

That is the production path-tracer completion pass: nested dielectric media and IOR stacks, TIR in the path integrator, colored-throughput Russian roulette, deterministic/stratified/low-discrepancy/blue-noise streams, multithreaded tile scheduling, per-thread RNGs, false-sharing-safe film accumulation, HDR output, debug passes, convergence/reference tests, rays/sec and BVH profiling, packet/wavefront/GPU ray architectures, then a complete end-to-end path tracer with fault isolation across geometry, PDF, BRDF, visibility and accumulation.
Pass 8 completes Phase 21 — Ray Tracing, Monte Carlo Light Transport, Sampling, BVH Rendering, and Path Tracing.

The curriculum explicitly positions M125 as the “make transport survive real materials, real randomness and real CPU execution” module and M126 as the “prove it, profile it, restructure it for parallel hardware, and know exactly where it is broken” module.
Now we make that system survive scenes like:
